questions.q: As per Section 5(b) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, deposits accepted for lending or investment are repayable on demand or otherwise, and withdrawal is made by which means?
questions.explain: Section 5(b) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 defines banking as accepting deposits repayable on demand or otherwise, and withdrawal by cheque, draft, order or otherwise.

questions.q: According to John Paget's definition, what constitutes a person as a 'Customer' of a bank?
options: A person who has taken a loan from the bank
A person who has deposited money only once
A person who has an account with the bank, whether fixed or savings, and has dealing of a banking nature
Any person who enters a bank branch for enquiry
questions.explain: John Paget defined a Customer as 'a person who has an account with a bank, whether fixed or savings, and has dealing of banking nature.'

questions.q: John Paget's definition of Customer, based on transactions of deposit and withdrawal of money at frequent intervals, is popularly known as what?
questions.explain: The document states this definition of Customer 'is popularly known as the Duration Theory.'

questions.q: The banking relationship between a bank and its customer is established as a contract governed by which Act?
questions.explain: The slide states that banking relationship is a contract between the Bank and the Customer, and refers to the Indian Contract Act, 1872 for establishing the relationship.

questions.q: As per the Indian Contract Act 1872, which of the following persons is NOT legally competent to enter into a contract with a bank?
options: A major person of sound mind
A drunken person who is not in good sense
A person not disqualified by any law
A person who is not insolvent
questions.explain: The material states that a drunken person is not legally competent to enter into a contract, and one should be in good sense while opening an account.

questions.q: As per the Indian Contract Act 1872, at what age does an individual become 'major' and legally competent to enter into a valid contract?
questions.explain: The individual should be major, i.e. of 18 years of age, to be competent to enter into a valid contract.

questions.q: Besides proof of identity, residential address and photographs, what else must a person furnish while opening a deposit account?
options: Initial deposit not less than the prescribed minimum
questions.explain: The prescribed account opening form requires proof of identity and address, photographs, and an initial deposit not less than the prescribed minimum.

questions.q: As per RBI's guidance mentioned in the training material, what is NOT necessary for opening a new bank account?
options: Introduction by an existing account holder
questions.explain: RBI has informed that introduction is not necessary for opening of accounts, so banks should not insist on introduction of an existing customer while opening a new account.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed under the 'Personal accounts' category of customer types in the training material?
questions.explain: Under 'Personal accounts' the material lists Single Individual, Joint Individual, Minor Account, Illiterate Person, Blind Person, and Pardanashin women.

questions.q: What is the stated purpose of accepting deposits of money from the public, as per the definition of banking under Section 5(b) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949?
options: For the purpose of lending or investment
questions.explain: Banking is defined as 'accepting for the purpose of lending or investment, of deposits of money from public.'

questions.q: A single individual account is a purely personal account that is normally operated upon by whom?
questions.explain: The document states this account 'is normally operated upon by the account holder himself.'

questions.q: In a single individual account, how can the account holder authorize another person to operate the account?
options: It is not permitted under any circumstance
By a verbal instruction to the branch staff
By giving Mandate or Power of Attorney
questions.explain: The account holder 'may authorize another person to operate the account by giving him Mandate or Power of Attorney.'

questions.q: Why is it desirable to obtain proper nomination on a single individual account?
options: To avoid legal complications that may arise after the death of the account holder
To reduce the minimum balance requirement
To enable joint operation of the account
questions.explain: The material states nomination is obtained 'in order to avoid legal complications that may arise after the death of the account holder.'

questions.q: A joint account of more than one individual is opened for operational convenience or to avoid legal complications arising from which event?
options: Death of one of the joint account holders
questions.explain: Joint accounts are opened 'for operational convenience or to avoid legal complications upon death of one of the joint account holders.'

questions.q: In a joint account, who can change addition/deletion of a name, make a material alteration, close the account, or change operational instructions?
options: The bank alone, at its discretion
questions.explain: The material states these actions 'can be changed by all the account holders jointly.'

questions.q: In a joint account operated with the instruction 'Former or Survivor,' who alone can change or revoke the operating instructions?
options: Any one of the account holders
questions.explain: The material states that in joint accounts with 'Former or Survivor' instructions, 'instructions can be changed/revoked only by Former.'

questions.q: In a joint account with 'Either or Survivor' operating instructions, who can request a Stop Payment on a cheque?
options: Any one of the account holders
questions.explain: As per the Joint Account Summary table, Stop Payment under 'Either or Survivor' instructions can be requested by 'Any one' account holder.

questions.q: In a joint account with 'Former or Survivor' instructions, payment on maturity of a Fixed Deposit Receipt (FDR) can be made to whom?
options: Any one of the account holders
questions.explain: The Joint Account Summary table shows that for 'Former or Survivor' accounts, payment on maturity of an FDR is made to 'Only Former.'

questions.q: Under all three joint account operating modes shown in the training material (Either or Survivor, Former or Survivor, and Joint Operation), what is required for premature payment of an FDR?
questions.explain: The Joint Account Summary table shows 'All jointly' is required for premature payment of FDR under all three operating modes.

questions.q: In 'Joint Operation' mode with a nomination in place, once all original account holders have died, to whom is payment made?
options: Only to the bank as unclaimed deposit
The survivor and legal heirs, till any of the survivor is alive
Only to the nominee's own legal heirs
questions.explain: The Joint Account Summary table shows payment in case of nomination under 'Joint Operation' goes to 'Survivor and legal heirs till any of survivor is alive.'

questions.q: As per Section 3 of the Indian Majority Act, at what age does a person normally attain majority, except when a guardian is appointed by a Court?
questions.explain: Section 3 of the Indian Majority Act says a person attains majority at 18, except where a guardian is appointed by a Court, where the age of majority is 21.

questions.q: As per the Indian Contract Act, what is the legal status of a contract entered into with a minor?
options: The contract is valid only for savings accounts
The contract is valid but voidable
The contract is valid if witnessed
questions.explain: A minor is not under a legal capacity to enter into a contract, and therefore any contract with a minor is void.

questions.q: Section 6(a) of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 recognizes which persons as the natural guardian of a Hindu minor?
options: Either of the parents, father or mother
questions.explain: Section 6(a) of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 recognizes that either of the parents, father or mother, can be the natural guardian.

questions.q: What type of account should NOT be opened for a minor, as per the training material?
questions.explain: The material states 'No Current Account should be opened' for a minor.

questions.q: In a self-operated minor account, who makes the nomination since the minor cannot?
options: No nomination is possible for minor accounts
questions.explain: A minor cannot make a nomination in a self-operated minor account; nomination is done by the guardian of the minor.

questions.q: Literate minors above what age may be allowed to open and operate savings bank accounts independently, subject to bank-fixed limits?
questions.explain: The material states 'Literate Minors above the age of 10 years may be now allowed to open and operate savings bank accounts independently.'

questions.q: When a minor attains the age of majority, who should operate the account?
options: Only the guardian, until a fresh mandate is filed
The bank operates it in trust until further notice
The guardian continues to operate jointly with the minor
The minor alone; the guardian should not be allowed to operate the account
questions.explain: On attaining majority, the minor alone can operate the account and the guardian should not be allowed to operate the account.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the three types of guardian listed in the training material?
questions.explain: The three types of guardian listed are Natural Guardian, Testamentary Guardian (appointed by will), and Legal Guardian (appointed by court).

questions.q: Under Mohammedan Law, who can act as the natural guardian of a Muslim minor's account?
options: Either parent, as under Hindu law
Any senior family member chosen by consensus
The father (or father's father), not the mother
questions.explain: Accounts of Mohammedan minors are operated by the father, who is the natural guardian; the mother cannot act as natural guardian under Mohammedan Law.

questions.q: In the case of a deceased minor's account, to whom is the balance payable, and on production of what document?
options: To the bank as unclaimed deposit
To the minor's legal heirs without any documentation
To the natural guardian only after 10 years
To the guardian, upon production of the death certificate
questions.explain: In case of death of the minor, the balance is payable to the guardian upon production of the death certificate.

questions.q: How is an 'Illiterate person' defined in the training material?
options: A person below 18 years of age
A person who cannot read or write
A person without a bank account
A person who cannot sign in English
questions.explain: The material states 'Illiterate person is a person who cannot read or write.'

questions.q: Before opening an account for an illiterate person, who must introduce them to the branch?
options: An existing literate account holder of the branch
questions.explain: The material states 'The illiterate person will have to be introduced by an existing literate account holder of the branch.'

questions.q: Which thumb impression is normally obtained from a male illiterate person for entering into an agreement with the bank?
questions.explain: The material states 'Normally, Left Hand Thumb impression (LHT) of male & Right Hand Thumb impression (RHT) of female is to be obtained.'

questions.q: Who can attest the thumb impression of an illiterate person on the account opening form?
options: A judicial officer or bank official or a witness who is also an account holder of the bank
Any relative of the account holder
A neighbour of the account holder
questions.explain: The material states the thumb impression 'has to be attested by a judicial officer or bank official or any witness who is also the account holder of the bank.'

questions.q: How many witnesses are required for nomination in the case of an illiterate customer?
questions.explain: The material states 'Two witnesses required for nomination' for illiterate persons.

questions.q: For an illiterate customer, who is NOT permitted to fill up the withdrawal slip?
options: No bank employee should fill it up
The illiterate customer's own family member
A witness known to the bank
questions.explain: The material states 'No bank employee should fill up the withdrawal slip for the illiterate customer and he can be assisted by any other customer of the bank.'

questions.q: For a blind person's account, who must witness the signature or thumb impression on the account opening form?
options: Only a family member of the blind person
A person who certifies that the contents of the form were explained to the blind person in his presence
questions.explain: The material states the signature/thumb impression 'to be witnessed by a person who should certify that contents of the A/c opening form were explained to the blind person in his presence.'

questions.q: A blind person should always visit the branch personally for which transaction, per the training material?
questions.explain: The material states 'He should always visit the branch for cash withdrawal.'

questions.q: What best describes a 'Pardanashin woman' according to the training material?
options: A woman who has never opened a bank account
A widow with no legal heirs
A woman above the age of 60
A lady who remains in complete seclusion and does not transact business with people other than her own family members
questions.explain: The material defines a Pardanashin woman as 'a lady who remains in complete seclusion & does not transact any business with people other than her own family members.'

questions.q: Normally, what type of account is NOT opened in the name of a Pardanashin woman?
questions.explain: The material states 'Normally no current account is opened' for a Pardanashin woman.

questions.q: As per Hindu law, which communities can form a Hindu Undivided Family (HUF)?
options: All Indian citizens regardless of religion
questions.explain: The material states 'As per Hindu law, the Hindus, Sikhs & Jains can form HUF.'

questions.q: HUF is governed by two schools of thought. In Bengal, HUF is governed by which law?
questions.explain: The material states 'In Bengal, it is governed by Dayabhag law; in other parts of India, it is governed by Mitakshara Law.'

questions.q: In an HUF, the joint owners are known by what term?
questions.explain: The material states 'Joint owner of HUF are known as coparceners.'

questions.q: Who manages the HUF property, as the senior-most major male member of the family?
questions.explain: The material states 'HUF property is managed by senior most major male member called Manager or Karta.'

questions.q: As per which Supreme Court judgement, cited in the training material, can an HUF NOT enter into a partnership?
questions.explain: The material states 'HUF cannot enter into a partnership as per Supreme Court judgement of 1998.'

questions.q: What document must be signed by the Karta and all the coparceners when opening an HUF account?
questions.explain: The material states 'Joint Hindu Family Letter (CD-115) to be signed by Karta & all the coparceners.'

questions.q: If the PAN of the HUF is not available, whose PAN should at least be obtained?
options: No PAN is required in this case
questions.explain: The material states 'PAN of HUF required, if not at least Karta should have PAN.'

questions.q: Does the death of a coparcener dissolve the HUF?
options: Only if all coparceners agree to dissolve it
Yes, the HUF is automatically dissolved
No, death of a coparcener does not dissolve the HUF
Only if the deceased was the Karta
questions.explain: The material states 'Death of coparcener does not dissolve HUF,' though it is advisable to obtain a fresh CD-115 letter on such an event.

questions.q: From when are female descendants included as coparceners in an HUF, per the training material?
questions.explain: The material states the HUF consists of a common ancestor and 'his all male & female (female from Sept. 2005) descendents up to 3 generation next to him.'

questions.q: Under which sections of the Income Tax Act can an HUF account avail tax rebates and deductions, per the training material?
questions.explain: The material states 'According to IT act, tax rebates and deductions can be availed under sections 80C, 88 and 80L for HUF account.'

questions.q: In a proprietorship firm, the business is wholly owned by whom?
questions.explain: The material states 'Business is wholly owned by an individual' in a proprietorship firm.

questions.q: In law, what is the relationship between a proprietor and the proprietorship firm?
options: The firm is taxed separately from the proprietor
There is no difference between the proprietor and the firm
They are two distinct legal entities
The firm has limited liability separate from the proprietor
questions.explain: The material states 'In law, there is no difference between proprietor & the firm.'

questions.q: What must be obtained from the proprietor in the bank's prescribed format when opening a proprietorship account?
options: Proprietorship letter in the bank's Performa
questions.explain: The material states 'Proprietorship letter in bank's Performa is to be obtained.'

questions.q: A proprietorship firm's account is, in all respects, an account in the name of whom?
options: An individual, operated upon by the proprietor on behalf of the firm
A joint venture of multiple owners
questions.explain: The material states 'In all respects, it is an account in the name of an individual only except that it is operated upon by the proprietor on behalf of firm.'

questions.q: What registration does the training material state a proprietorship firm should have?
questions.explain: The material states 'The firm should have GST No.'

questions.q: In case of a proprietorship firm's debts, against which assets do creditors have recourse?
options: Both the assets of the firm and the private assets of the proprietor
Only the private assets of the proprietor's family members
Only the assets of the firm
No recourse is available since liability is limited
questions.explain: The material states 'Creditors have recourse not only against assets of the firm but also against private assets of the proprietor.'

questions.q: In what capacity must a proprietor execute security documents for the bank?
options: Only as Proprietor on behalf of the firm
As Proprietor on behalf of the firm, as well as in his individual capacity
questions.explain: The material states the bank insists 'that proprietor should execute the security documents in the capacity as Proprietor on behalf of the firm as well as in his individual capacity.'

questions.q: How can a proprietor authorise another person to operate the firm's bank account?
options: It is not permitted for proprietorship firms
Through Mandate or Power of Attorney
questions.explain: The material states 'Proprietor can authorise another person to operate the account through Mandate or Power of Attorney.'

questions.q: Along with the KYC Official Valid Documents of the proprietor, how many additional documents from the prescribed list must be obtained to establish proof of proprietorship?
questions.explain: The material states 'Along with KYC Official Valid Documents of Proprietor, any two of the followings required.'

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as an acceptable document to establish proof of proprietorship of a firm?
options: Trust deed and a certificate from the Charity Commission
Certificate/licence issued by the municipal authorities under the Shop and Establishment Act
questions.explain: Among the documents listed for proprietorship proof is a 'Certificate/licence issued by the municipal authorities under Shop and Establishment Act.'

questions.q: As per the Partnership Act 1932, partnership is defined as the relation between persons who have agreed to do what?
options: Share losses of a business equally
Share profits of a business carried on by all or any one of them acting for all
questions.explain: The material states 'Partnership is the relation between persons who have agreed to share profits of business carried on by all or any one them acting for all (Partnership Act 1932).'

questions.q: Which two documents, referenced by Circular Letter No 2014-15/102 dated 08.10.2014, must be obtained for a partnership firm account?
options: Certificate of Incorporation and Board Resolution
questions.explain: The material states 'Registration Certificate and Partnership deed to be obtained (Cir Letter No 2014-15/102 dated 08.10.2014).'

questions.q: As per the Companies Act 2013, what is the maximum number of partners now allowed in a partnership firm, excluding minors?
questions.explain: The material states 'As per Companies Act 2013, Maximum number of partner can be up to 100 (excluding minor) in a firm.'

questions.q: Before the Companies Act 2013 raised the limit, what was the maximum number of partners permitted in a partnership firm carrying on banking business?
questions.explain: The material states the earlier number was 'restricted to 20 for other businesses & 10 for Banking business.'

questions.q: Can a minor be admitted as a full partner in a partnership firm?
options: Yes, a minor can be a full partner if the guardian consents
Yes, a minor can be a partner after age 15
No, a minor cannot be a partner, but can be admitted for his benefit in an existing partnership firm
It depends on the amount of capital contributed
questions.explain: The material states 'A minor cannot a partner, but he can be admitted for his benefit in an existing partnership firm.'

questions.q: In a partnership account with no clear-cut operational instructions in the deed, how should the account be operated?
questions.explain: The material states 'In the absence of clear cut operational instructions, account to be operated upon by all the partners jointly.'

questions.q: Can any one partner stop payment of a cheque issued by another partner of the same firm?
options: Yes, any partner can stop a cheque issued by another partner
No, only the issuing partner can stop it
Only the Managing Partner can stop it
No, only all partners jointly can stop it
questions.explain: The material states 'Any partner can stop cheque issued by another partner.'

questions.q: Cheques favouring the partnership firm can be deposited into which account, per the training material?
options: Only the firm's account, not into the individual accounts of partners
Any account nominated by a majority of the partners
Any account at the bank's discretion
questions.explain: The material states 'Cheques favouring firm can not be deposited in the individual accounts of partners.'

questions.q: As per the Supreme Court judgement of 1998 referenced in the training material, which entity cannot enter into a partnership?
questions.explain: The material states 'HUF cannot enter into a partnership as per Supreme Court judgement of 1998.'

questions.q: If a partner's account balance is in debit at the time of his death, retirement or insolvency, what should the bank do?
options: Stop the account, and open a fresh account only after fresh sanction of limit
Have the remaining partners automatically inherit the debit balance
Write off the debit balance immediately
Allow the account to continue unchanged
questions.explain: The material states 'In case of death/retirement/insolvency of a partner a/c should be stopped, if the balance is in debit and a fresh account should opened after fresh sanction of limit.'

questions.q: A Limited Liability Partnership (LLP) is governed by which Act?
questions.explain: The material states 'LLP is governed by limited liability partnership Act 2008.'

questions.q: What is the minimum number of designated partners required to form an LLP?
questions.explain: The material states 'Minimum 2 designated partner, no limit on maximum No. of Partners.'

questions.q: Does the death of a partner affect the existence of an LLP?
options: No, an LLP has perpetual succession and continues to exist
Yes, unless a new partner joins within 30 days
Only if the deceased was a designated partner
Yes, the LLP is automatically dissolved
questions.explain: The material states an LLP 'has perpetual succession (death of a partner does not affect the existence of LLP).'

questions.q: Can an LLP raise funds from the public?
options: No, an LLP cannot raise funds from the public
Yes, freely, like a public limited company
questions.explain: The material states 'LLP can not raise fund from public.'

questions.q: What is the minimum and maximum number of members allowed in a Private Limited Company?
questions.explain: The material states members of a Private Limited Company are 'Min. – 2 members, Max. - 200 members.'

questions.q: What is the minimum number of members required to form a Public Limited Company?
questions.explain: The material states 'Members – Min. 7 & Max – No limit' for a Public Limited Company.

questions.q: The names of Public Limited Companies must end with which word?
questions.explain: The material states 'Names of the companies ends with the words "Limited"' for Public Limited Companies.

questions.q: What must a Public Limited Company obtain before it can commence any type of business?
questions.explain: The material states 'Certificate of commencement of business is must to do any type of business' for a Public Limited Company.

questions.q: As per the training material, a 'Government Company' is one in which not less than what percentage of paid-up share capital is held by the Central or State Government(s)?
questions.explain: The material defines a Government Company as one where 'not less than fifty one percent of the paid-up share capital is held by the Central Government, or by any State Government or Governments.'

questions.q: Under Section 3(1) of the Companies Act 2013, a One Person Company (OPC) is a company with how many persons as its member?
questions.explain: The material states 'An OPC means a company with only one person as its member [section 3(1) of 2013 Act].'

questions.q: Who issues the Certificate of Incorporation to a company?
options: Ministry of Corporate Affairs Secretary directly
questions.explain: The material states the Certificate of Incorporation is 'Issued by Registrar of Companies.'

questions.q: Is a Certificate of Commencement of Business required for a Private Limited Company?
options: Yes, but only for companies with paid-up capital above Rs 1 lakh
Only if the company has more than 50 members
Yes, it is mandatory for all companies
No, it is not required since its shares are closely held and it can commence business on incorporation
questions.explain: The material states 'Certificate of commencement of business is not required by Private Ltd. Co. as it's shares are closely held & it can commence business on it's incorporation.'

questions.q: Which document is described as the company's 'fundamental & unalterable law,' embodying its name, authorized capital, objectives and shareholders' liability?
questions.explain: The material describes the Memorandum of Association as the 'Company's fundamental & unalterable law' embodying name, authorized capital, objectives and liability of shareholders.

questions.q: Which document is also known as the 'Document of Indoor Management' and regulates internal management, directors' powers, meeting conduct and borrowing procedures?
questions.explain: The material states Article of Association is 'Also known as Document of Indoor Management' with regulations controlling internal management of the company.

questions.q: A certified copy of the Board Resolution obtained by the bank should include details of which of the following?
options: Only the company's audited financial statements
Persons authorized to sign security documents and operate the bank account
questions.explain: The material states the Board Resolution should detail 'Persons who are authorized to sign the security documents & operate the Bank Account.'

questions.q: As per the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2015, is a company's common seal now compulsory on bank documents?
options: No, common seal of a company is not compulsory now
Yes, it is mandatory on all documents
questions.explain: The material states 'As per Companies (Amendment) Act, 2015, Common seal of company is not compulsory now.'

questions.q: What is the registered office of a company primarily important for, as per the training material?
options: It is the address at which all documents and notices may be served upon the company
It determines the company's tax rate
It is where shareholders' meetings must always be held
questions.explain: The material states the registered office 'is the address at which all the documents & notices may be served upon the company.'

questions.q: Cheques favouring a company should NOT be credited to which type of account, per the training material?
options: Personal accounts of the Directors or other officers of the company
questions.explain: The material states 'Cheques favouring company are not to be credited to the personal accounts of the Directors or other officers of the company.'

questions.q: Which unique identifier is listed among the documents to be obtained from a limited company?
options: Passport number of the Managing Director
PAN of each director's family members
questions.explain: The material lists 'Company Identification Number (CIN) of companies' among documents to be obtained from a limited company.

questions.q: Which document serves as conclusive proof of a company's incorporation and compliance of formalities by its promoters?
questions.explain: The material states the Certificate of Incorporation 'is conclusive proof for incorporation of the company & compliance of all formalities by promoters.'

questions.q: Trusts in India, as referenced in the training material, are governed by which Act?
questions.explain: The material states 'Trusts are governed by the Indian Trust Act, 1882.'

questions.q: A trust set up for the benefit of private individuals, rather than for a public charitable purpose, is called what?
questions.explain: The material states 'Trust may be public charitable trust or private trust (for benefit of private individuals).'

questions.q: Who manages a trust, per the training material?
questions.explain: The material states 'Trusts managed by trustees.'

questions.q: What must be examined before opening a trust account with the bank?
questions.explain: The material states 'Original Trust Deed to be examined before opening Account.'

questions.q: When the Trust Deed is silent about the operation of the account, how should the account be operated?
options: As per the bank's sole discretion
questions.explain: The material states 'When Trust Deed is silent about operation of the account, Account should be operated upon by all the trustees jointly.'

questions.q: For a public trust, which certificate must be examined and a copy kept on record?
options: Certificate of Registration under Public Trust Act
questions.explain: The material states 'Certificate of Registration under Public Trust Act to be examined & copy to be kept on record.'

questions.q: How are clubs and societies described in the training material?
options: Non-profit making organisations representing a group of persons
questions.explain: The material states 'Society & Clubs are non profit making organisations and represents a group of persons.'

questions.q: Under which Act(s) can clubs be registered, per the training material?
questions.explain: The material states 'Clubs can be registered under Society Act 1860, or Company Act 1956.'

questions.q: A club or society gets the status of a legal entity only after what event, per the training material?
options: Its incorporation in its own name
Registration with the Income Tax Department
questions.explain: The material states clubs and societies 'get the status of a legal entity only after their incorporation in their own name.'

questions.q: Cheques favouring a society, club or association should NOT be collected into which type of account?
options: Individual accounts of office bearers or employees
A joint account of all members
questions.explain: The material states 'Cheques favouring society, club, association not to be collected in individual A/Cs of office bearers or employees.'
